public final class TestEnum extends ValuedEnum {

    public static final int ONE_VALUE   = 1;

    public static final int NEG_VALUE   = -5;

    public static final TestEnum ONE = new TestEnum("ONE", ONE_VALUE);
    public static final TestEnum TWO = new TestEnum("TWO", TWO_VALUE);
    public static final TestEnum NEG = new TestEnum("NEG", NEG_VALUE);

    private TestEnum(String name, int value) {
        super(name, value);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Helper methods to expose the protected static getEnum() for tests

    /**
     * Wrapper around the protected {@code ValuedEnum.getEnum(Class,int)} method.

    }

/**
 * JUnit 4 test class for {@link ValuedEnum}.
 */
public class ValuedEnumTest {

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Basic functionality tests
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    @Test
    public void testGetValue() {
        assertEquals(TestEnum.ONE_VALUE, TestEnum.ONE.getValue());
        assertEquals(TestEnum.TWO_VALUE, TestEnum.TWO.getValue());
        assertEquals(TestEnum.NEG_VALUE, TestEnum.NEG.getValue());
    }

    @Test
    public void testCompareTo_SameClass() {
        // ONE < TWO
        assertTrue(TestEnum.ONE.compareTo(TestEnum.TWO) < 0);
        // TWO > ONE
        assertTrue(TestEnum.TWO.compareTo(TestEnum.ONE) > 0);
        // NEG < ONE
        assertTrue(TestEnum.NEG.compareTo(TestEnum.ONE) < 0);
        // Equality
        assertEquals(0, TestEnum.ONE.compareTo(TestEnum.ONE));
    }

    @Test
    public void testToString_FormatAndCaching() {
        String expected = "TestEnum[ONE=1]";
        String firstCall = TestEnum.ONE.toString();
        String secondCall = TestEnum.ONE.toString(); // should be cached
        assertEquals(expected, firstCall);
        assertSame(firstCall, secondCall); // same instance because of caching
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Tests for the protected static getEnum(Class,int) method (via wrapper)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    @Test
    public void testGetEnumByValue_Found() {
        assertSame(TestEnum.ONE, TestEnum.getEnumByValue(1));
        assertSame(TestEnum.TWO, TestEnum.getEnumByValue(2));
        assertSame(TestEnum.NEG, TestEnum.getEnumByValue(-5));
    }

    @Test
    public void testGetEnumByValue_NotFound() {
        assertNull(TestEnum.getEnumByValue(999));
    }

    @Test(expected = IllegalArgumentException.class)
    public void testGetEnumByValue_NullClass() {
        // Directly invoke the protected method via reflection to pass null class.
        // This reproduces the exact IllegalArgumentException thrown by the method.
        ValuedEnum.getEnum(null, 1);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Edge‑case / exception tests for compareTo
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    @Test(expected = NullPointerException.class)
    public void testCompareTo_NullArgument() {
        TestEnum.ONE.compareTo(null);
    }

    @Test(expected = ClassCastException.class)
    public void testCompareTo_WrongType() {
        // Create a dummy Enum subclass that is not a ValuedEnum
        class DummyEnum extends Enum {
            public DummyEnum(String name) { super(name); }
        }
        DummyEnum dummy = new DummyEnum("DUMMY");
        TestEnum.ONE.compareTo(dummy);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Additional utility tests (iterator, list) to ensure enum registration works
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    @Test
    public void testEnumListContainsAllConstants() {
        List<TestEnum> list = TestEnum.getEnumList();
        assertTrue(list.contains(TestEnum.ONE));
        assertTrue(list.contains(TestEnum.TWO));
        assertTrue(list.contains(TestEnum.NEG));
        // The list size should be exactly the number of defined constants
        assertEquals(3, list.size());
    }

    @Test
    public void testIteratorIteratesAllConstants() {
        Iterator<TestEnum> it = TestEnum.iterator();
        int count = 0;
        while (it.hasNext()) {
            TestEnum e = it.next();
            assertNotNull(e);
            count++;
        }
        assertEquals(3, count);
    }
}
